components.css: :host{--ink:#0b1b33;--ink2:#3b4a63;--ink3:#5c6b82;--ground:#f3f5f8;--stock:#ffffff;--rule:#c9d2de;--rule2:#e3e8ef;--act:#1d4ed8;--live:#0e7490;--live-fill:#0891b2;--alarm:#b91c1c;--wait:#b45309;--appr:#5b21b6;--hl:#fff4d6;font-family:Archivo,sans-serif;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;color:var(--ink);} .ds-head{background:var(--ink);color:#fff;padding:10px 14px;display:flex;gap:12px;align-items:baseline;flex-wrap:wrap;} .ds-head .no{font-size:1.5rem;font-weight:750;letter-spacing:-.01em;margin-right:auto;} .ds-head .lbl{font-size:.68rem;font-weight:650;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;color:#9fb2cf;} .ds-dkrow{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;border:1px solid var(--rule);border-top:0;background:var(--stock);} .ds-box{padding:9px 11px 8px;border-left:1px solid var(--rule);display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:6px;transition:opacity .3s ease-out,box-shadow .3s ease-out;} .ds-box:first-child{border-left:0;} .ds-dkrow.dim .ds-box:not(.live){opacity:.5;} .ds-box.live{outline:1px solid var(--live-fill);outline-offset:-1px;box-shadow:0 3px 14px rgba(11,27,51,.16);position:relative;} .ds-box .bh{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;border-bottom:1px solid var(--rule2);padding-bottom:6px;} .ds-box .bt{font-size:.92rem;font-weight:700;} .ds-box .bn{font-size:.66rem;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;color:var(--ink3);margin-right:4px;} .ds-box .ec{font-size:.66rem;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.1em;padding:0 5px;border:1px solid currentColor;color:var(--act);align-self:flex-start;} .ds-box ul{font-size:.82rem;color:var(--ink2);line-height:1.45;padding-left:16px;margin:0;} .ds-box .sig{border-top:1px dashed var(--rule);padding-top:5px;font-size:.72rem;color:var(--ink3);} .ds-box .sig i{font-style:normal;color:var(--ink);font-weight:600;}

narrative.overview:
Every screen is a printed shipping form: bills of lading, cargo manifests, dispatch dockets. White form stock sits on a cool grey ground, ruled with navy and blue-grey hairlines, and filled in navy ink with tabular figures. An orchestration run is a numbered docket. Each agent fills and signs its own box, the planner writes the plan into a ruled table, the narrator adds remarks, and a person stamps the authorisation box. The form is the interface; there are no floating cards, no pills and no gradients.

Density is high and deliberate, because the same sheet serves a projector audience and a working planner. Hierarchy comes from scale and weight contrast inside one variable family (Archivo), not from colour. Colour is reserved for meaning: blue for action, cyan for what is running now, violet for what waits on a human, amber for waiting and warning, red only for failure, rejection, stock-out and lateness. Motion is limited to three functional events: the running mark blinks, the filling box lifts while the others dim, and an authorisation stamp lands.
keyCharacteristics: Ruled form stock: 1px hairline seams, navy frame rules, zero radius on every form surface.
Field labels as small uppercase condensed caps above tabular-figure values.
States as printed square marks plus an uppercase word, never as rounded badges.
Enterprise identity by a 1px-ruled three-letter code chip in the enterprise colour.
Human authority as a double-ruled, rotated stamp.

rules.name: The Ink Not Green Rule
rules.body: Completed is a filled navy square. Green is not a state colour in this system; success is the absence of alarm.

rules.name: The Red Is Refusal Rule
rules.body: Alarm red appears only for failure, rejection, stock-out, late arrival and critical notices. If nothing is wrong, the screen holds no red.

rules.name: The Lamp Until Acknowledged Rule
rules.body: A changed plan row stays lit in change lamp, with the superseded value struck through, until a person acknowledges it.

rules.name: The Scale Contrast Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is carried by size, weight and width, never by colouring a heading.

rules.name: The Field Label Rule
rules.body: A label sits above its value in small condensed uppercase muted ink; the value is the loud element.

rules.name: The Lift Only While Filling Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Only the box currently being filled lifts, and only while it is running.

rules.name: The Zero Radius Rule
rules.body: Forms are cut paper: 0 radius. Only controls take 2px.

dos: Do draw every surface as ruled form stock: white fill, 1px hairline seams, 0 radius.
Do put a small uppercase condensed label above every figure, and set figures in tabular numerals.
Do express state with a square mark and an uppercase word, using the mark colours above.
Do identify an enterprise with its three-letter code chip wherever an agent or message appears.
Do keep changed plan rows lit in change lamp, with the old value struck through, until acknowledged.
Do keep Reject separated from Approve and secondary in weight.
Do honour reduced motion: no blink, no stamp landing.
donts: Don't build KPI card grids; use a ledger strip of ruled fields.
Don't round form surfaces or use pill badges for state.
Don't use green for success or red for anything except failure, rejection, stock-out, lateness and critical notices.
Don't add shadows to resting surfaces; only the box being filled lifts.
Don't use gradients or decorative animation.
Don't colour headings to create hierarchy; use size, weight and width.
